title: No lost Pauline letter to the Laodiceans — Col. 4 ambiguity
source_text: IX. Quod vero pertendunt Pontificiorum nonnulli periisse quandam epistolam Pauli ad Laodicenses, non habet ullum fundamentum: sed natum est ex ambiguitate, quae reperitur in verbis veteris interpretis ult. cap. Ep. ad Colos. Sic enim ibi legitur apud veterem interpretem, Quum lecta fuerit apud vos epistola, facite ut in Laodicensium Ecclesia legatur; & eam quae Laodicensium est vos quoque legatis. Per illam vero epistolam, quae ibi Laodicensium dicitur, intelligunt epistolam ad Laodicenses scriptam, cum revera ibi agatur de epistola scripta a Laodicensibus, ut manifestum est ex Graeco contextu, qui sic habet, καὶ τὴν ἐκ Λαοδικείας ἵνα καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀναγνῶτε, & scriptam a Laodicea vos quoque legatis. Nam certe nullus est Graece tantisper intelligens qui ignorare possit τὴν ἐκ Λαοδικείας significare epistolam scriptam e Laodicea, non vero ad Laodicenses.
pass_a_gloss: But what some of the Pontiffs claim — that some epistle of Paul to the Laodiceans has perished — has no foundation: it was born from an ambiguity found in the words of the old translator at the last chapter of the Epistle to the Colossians. For thus it is read in the old translator: When this epistle shall have been read among you, cause that it be read also in the church of the Laodiceans; and that you likewise read the epistle of Laodicea. By that epistle which is there called of the Laodiceans, they understand an epistle written to the Laodiceans, whereas in truth the text is about an epistle written by the Laodiceans, as is plain from the Greek context, which has: καὶ τὴν ἐκ Λαοδικείας ἵνα καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀναγνῶτε, and the one written from Laodicea you also should read. For surely no one who understands Greek even a little can fail to know that τὴν ἐκ Λαοδικείας means an epistle written from Laodicea, not to the Laodiceans.
pass_b_english: Rome's 'lost letter to Laodicea' rests on a Latin ambiguity in Col. 4, not on a vanished Canon.
The Vulgate's 'epistle of the Laodiceans' is read as a letter to them; the Greek says a letter from Laodicea.
τὴν ἐκ Λαοδικείας means written from Laodicea — anyone with a little Greek can see it.
So the lost-Laodiceans proof for an incomplete Canon falls with the mistranslation.
